regions.name: Java
visual_identifiers: most densely populated island on earth
specific Javanese batik and cultural elements

state_distinguishers.Jakarta: Megacity infrastructure, TransJakarta BRT buses distinctive, very dense urban
state_distinguishers.Yogyakarta: Cultural capital feel, Borobudur and Prambanan temple proximity, more traditional atmosphere
state_distinguishers.East_Java: Bromo volcano area distinctive, more rural feel than west

regions.route_sign_clues: Trans-Java Toll Road running east-west. Green and white Indonesian highway signs.
regions.gemini_hint: TransJakarta red BRT buses = Jakarta. Borobudur Buddhist temple = Yogyakarta area. Bromo volcanic landscape = East Java. Most densely packed urban = Java generally.
common_false_positives: Volcanic peaks — shared with Sumatra and Bali

regions.name: Sumatra
visual_identifiers: palm oil plantation rows very common

state_distinguishers.North_Sumatra: Lake Toba caldera visible, Batak cultural architecture, Medan city infrastructure
state_distinguishers.West_Sumatra: Minangkabau curved roof architecture very distinctive, Padang city
state_distinguishers.Aceh: Most Islamic province, Arabic script alongside Indonesian, northernmost tip

regions.gemini_hint: Curved buffalo horn roofs = West Sumatra/Minangkabau. Lake caldera = North Sumatra/Lake Toba. Arabic script + Islamic architecture = Aceh. Palm oil rows = Sumatra or Borneo.
common_false_positives: Palm oil plantations — also in Malaysian Borneo and peninsular Malaysia

regions.name: Kalimantan (Borneo)
visual_identifiers: palm oil and coal mining infrastructure
specific Dayak cultural elements in places
new capital city Nusantara under construction in East Kalimantan

state_distinguishers.East_Kalimantan: New capital Nusantara construction visible, oil and gas infrastructure, Balikpapan city
state_distinguishers.South_Kalimantan: Banjarmasin floating market infrastructure, more developed than other provinces

regions.route_sign_clues: Road infrastructure much less developed than Java.
regions.gemini_hint: New capital construction = East Kalimantan. Floating market = South Kalimantan. Very remote rainforest = Central Kalimantan.
common_false_positives: Rainforest and rivers — hard to distinguish provinces

regions.name: Bali and Nusa Tenggara
visual_identifiers: Komodo dragon warning signs in Flores

state_distinguishers.Bali: Hindu temple gates (candi bentar), very distinctive carved stone decoration, rice terraces, tourist infrastructure
state_distinguishers.Lombok: More Islamic than Bali, Rinjani volcano visible
state_distinguishers.Flores: Komodo dragon signage, very rugged dry terrain

regions.route_sign_clues: Bali has specific tourist road infrastructure.
regions.gemini_hint: Hindu temple gates = Bali almost certainly. Komodo warning signs = Flores/East Nusa Tenggara. Rinjani volcano = Lombok.
common_false_positives: Rice terraces — also in Java and Philippines

regions.name: Sulawesi and Eastern Indonesia
visual_identifiers: Torajan boat-shaped roof architecture in South Sulawesi
Papua has unique tribal cultural elements

state_distinguishers.South_Sulawesi: Torajan boat-shaped roofs very distinctive, Makassar city
state_distinguishers.Papua: Most remote province, tribal cultural elements, very undeveloped infrastructure

regions.route_sign_clues: Very limited road infrastructure in eastern Indonesia.
regions.gemini_hint: Boat-shaped roofs = South Sulawesi/Toraja area. Extremely remote tribal = Papua. Makassar urban = South Sulawesi.
common_false_positives: Tropical coast — shared across eastern Indonesia
